notes.title: Exophobia: Fire & Ice Expedition - Content Update Announcement
notes.content:
Just announced during BoomStock, a new content update that will bring a whole new adventure!

[i]Set in the world of Exophobia, play a new short adventure, set prior to the events in the main game.
Play as the I.S.A ship scientist, as you explore a cave deep in the alien planet. Fight new enemies and face new challenges - can you make it out alive?[/i]

Check out the clip here: [previewyoutube=Lm-IJQ33pYA;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


It's still very early in development, but it has been fun revisiting the game world :)
This short adventure will bring fresh mechanics, so if you want MORE Exophobia, don't miss this update!
I had the idea for this update ever since mid-development of the main game. I was not sure if I would include it as a separate demo, content update or paid DLC. Now that I got a new boost of energy to work on games again, I decided to include it as a free update to thank all the players that supported Exophobia.

This is for you! Stay tuned!
Zarc

notes.title: Exophobia Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hey there!
As promised and part of FPS Fest, the demo has been sligthly improved to better reflect the quality of the final game. Testing has been crucial to find these small quirks and how to adjust them. You may not notice any differences, so let me present you the changes in this new version:

[list]
[*] Some language errors fixed.
[*] Disk image in the corner to indicate a loading time.
[*] [i]"Sci-fi"[/i] font option is now a more readable font in the terminal.
[*] Map no longer starts to fade right away. Only when it reaches the last point in the battery.
[*] Clickable buttons and levers now blink to indicate you can use an action on them.
[*] You can now dash forward even if not holding a direction. Also, more i-frames!
[*] Difficulty curve in the first part of the game has been adjusted. Less enemies before you get the first upgrade (for me where the fun of the game comes).
[*] The boss now stays locked in the same vulnerable move until you hit. I made it that way so you can more easily guess what you have to do and so you don't have to wait until he cycles through all moves again to hit him.
[/list]

Can't even tell how long I have been revising this first part of the game, but I know it's the most important part to get right, so I hope these changes please all of you and incentivize you to keep playing!
Let me know what you think. 
More news coming soon!
Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]

notes.title: Exophobia at Metroidvania Fusion!
notes.content:
From March 4th to 11th, Exophobia is joining more than 170 other games in a Steam event all about metroidvanias, hosted by Ravenage Games.

Here you will find discounts in the most iconic games of the genre, or play demos of upcoming gems!

[b]Why is Exophobia considered a metroidvania?[/b]
Most metroidvania fans will argue that a metroidvania (metroid + castlevania for those who don't know) needs to be a sidescroller. 
My idea with Exophobia was to mix metroidvania progression with a first person shooter and I think it fits pretty well! Let's see, for example, where a Metroid game and Wolfenstein 3d can meet in the middle:

[list]
[*] Labyrinthic non-linear levels with gates that can only be opened with upgrades? [i]check[/i]
[*] Secrets around every corner or hidden wall that reward the player with powerups or easter eggs? [i]check[/i]
[*] Different biomes with different enemies and boss fights? [i]check[/i]
[/list]
Exophobia features all of this and more elements from both genres, like metroidvania checkpoints and fast paced shooter combat from first person shooters.

Let me know what you think! Meanwhile, play the demo and enjoy all the other available games in the event :)
Happy exploration!
Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/0323b64e5cd314f5e05bd34268c37553469572ea.png[/img]

notes.title: Going Rogue: A Festival of Persistence - Can a FPS also be a Metroidvania?
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
Exophobia has been selected to be part of a Steam festival all about roguelikes, rogue-lites, souls-likes and [b]metroidvanias[/b], called [url=https://store.steampowered.com/category/going_rogue/]Going Rogue: A Festival of Persistence [/url]!

I was a bit surprised to see Steam inviting me to be part of a festival with this name, until I saw metroidvanias were part of the list of celebrated types of games. And metroidvania is one of Exophobia's most prominent tag, and this is where the game's inclusion might start to sound controversial. But here is how I designed Exophobia to feel like a METROIDVANIA FPS! 

Steam defines games eligible for this festival with "[i]These games generally share mechanics of repeating parts of the game again and again, or re-treading ground once the player has gained enough experience or equipment."[/i]

Even though metroidvanias are often thought as 2D platformers, progression in Exophobia was designed to feature these ideas as an FPS with no verticality (quite a challenge!).
The gameplay happens inside the spaceship, a giant map with multiple floors each having their own characteristics (look, enemies, objects,...), with multiple gated areas, designed to push exploration. The player progresses through the game by finding upgrades, that improve combat mechanics as well as uncover areas that were locked before. The more you progress, the more the map opens up, and you might even find secrets that you can now access with your new abilities as you backtrack to find your next one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/9d0e89bbc337ccd303dccd8b03fc79a1d2e625d0.png[/img]

Besides this larger progression loop, you can also find other gated areas with one-way doors, key cards, movement challenging areas and even boss fights can unlock something on the map! You also have to save often in checkpoints, because that's where you return when you die, something you also see in metroidvanias.

So, in brief:
[list]
[*]One giant map with different themed areas and checkpoints.[i]Check[/i]
[*]A clear player power arc and enjoyable movement. [i]Check[/i]
[*]Gates, boss fights and hidden secrets to reward exploration. [i]Check[/i]
[/list]

Of course, feel free to give your own opinions on the subject :)
Have some great runs with the festival,
Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]

You just made this event so amazing and helped a lot! And congrats to everyone who beat the demo, it turns out it was not as easy as I thought.. (as always). 
[/b]
[/h3]

You can always join the [url=https://discord.gg/Qb5Kd3p]Zarc Attack Discord[/url] to chat with me and other fans. 

Also, due to some requests,[h3][b] I will keep the demo available for the next couple of days.[/b]
[/h3] If you didn't had the chance to play it, you can do it now, for maybe the end of this week. After that I want to take it out, because I will focus on all your feedback and turn Exophobia into an even better game than this demo shows!

Here's some extra challenges if you want to replay the demo:
[list]
[*]  Collect all discs (5/5)
[*]  Collect all health upgrades (3/3)
[*]  Push an enemy into the conveyor belt end
[*]  Lure an alien into some lasers
[*]  Find the hidden helmet powerup (3/3)
[*]  Beat the final boss with no damage
[/list]

Thank you once again, Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]
